# Validation against the SNMMI Dosimetry Challenge

radot doses are computed on the clinical images of the [SNMMI 177Lu Dosimetry Challenge](https://doi.org/10.2967/jnumed.122.265094) and compared with the results of the challenge participants.

**There is no ground truth**: the reference is the distribution of the participants' results (median, interquartile range IQR, quartile coefficient of dispersion QCD = (Q3 − Q1) / (Q3 + Q1)), from Brosch-Lenz et al., J Nucl Med 2023;64:1109, Supplemental Table 1. This is complementary to the [validation against Monte Carlo](7_validation_opengate.md): OpenGATE checks the physics with a known activity, the challenge checks the workflow on real images against the community.

## The challenge

Two patients treated with ¹⁷⁷Lu-DOTATATE, imaged with SPECT/CT at 4 time points (Siemens Intevo, xSPECT Quant, images in Bq/mL).

| Patient | Sex | Injected (MBq) | Imaging days | Organs | Lesions |
|---|---|--:|---|---|--:|
| A | male | 7210 | 0, 1, 4, 5 | liver, ltkidney, rtkidney, spleen | 2 |
| B | female | 7305 | 0, 1, 4, 8 | liver, ltkidney, rtkidney | 4 |

Tasks:

| Task | Input | Left to the participant | radot |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | serial SPECT/CT | segmentation, registration, fit, dose | not yet |
| T2, T3 | planar (+ 1 SPECT/CT) | everything | out of scope |
| T4 | serial SPECT/CT + VOIs at each time point | time integration, dose | below |
| T5 | time-integrated activity (TIA) map + VOIs | dose only | below |

## T5: dose from the TIA map

- **Input**: the TIA map provided by the challenge (Bq·s/mL, registered to the first SPECT, unit `bqsml` in the sidecar) and the organ and lesion VOIs of the first time point.
- **Mass**: from the CT of the first time point resampled to the TIA grid (density from the Hounsfield units).
- **`svalue`**: TIA in the VOI × OpenDose self S-value, scaled to the VOI mass (ICRP-110 male phantom for A, female for B). Organs only: there are no S-values for lesions.
- **`ldm`**: local energy deposition of the voxel TIA, mean in the VOI.
- **`gate`**: [OpenGATE](https://github.com/OpenGATE/opengate) Monte Carlo (`opengate_dose_rate`, Lu-177, electrons and photons) with the TIA map as source and the CT on the TIA grid; the dose-rate map is used with `radot dose --dose-rate-map` (dose = map × TIA / simulated activity). Includes the photon self- and cross-doses. GATE unc.: statistical uncertainty (one standard deviation) of the VOI mean.
- **Total kidney**: mass-weighted mean of the left and right kidney doses.
- **Difference**: (radot − participants' median) / median; ✗ when radot is outside the participants' interquartile range [Q1–Q3].

Absorbed doses in Gy for the whole treatment cycle (the TIA map is integrated over time).

Findings:

- All organs and lesions (except the liver of A, see below) are within 6.5 % of the participants' median; outside the IQR: A Lesion2 (gate), A Kidneys (total) (ldm), A Kidneys (total) (gate).
- **Liver of A**: the liver VOI contains lesion 1. The participants' spread (QCD 32 %, the largest of T5) matches two liver definitions: the VOI as given gives 2.39 Gy (median 2.25 Gy), the liver without the lesions 1.32 Gy (Q1 1.27 Gy). For B the lesions inside the liver are small.
- The doses of A are a few percent below the median, those of B close to it. The Monte Carlo (`gate`, with photons and cross-doses) is as low as `svalue`: the cause is not the dose model but most likely the mass convention (see [Effect of the mass](#effect-of-the-mass)).
- `ldm` is 1–2 % below `svalue`: no photon self-dose.
- `gate` vs `ldm`: -2.0 to +4.2 %; `gate` vs `svalue` (organs): -1.6 to +0.6 %. The Monte Carlo adds the photons and the cross-doses, and transports the electrons beyond the voxel and the VOI boundary.

## Effect of the mass

radot computes the VOI mass from the CT (density = 1 + HU/1000, CT resampled to the TIA grid). Many dosimetry tools use the VOI volume times a fixed density instead, often 1.00 or 1.06 g/mL. The participants' masses are not published. All the methods divide by the mass, so the dose scales as 1 / mass: below, the radot dose (`svalue`, or `ldm` for the lesions) recomputed with the other mass conventions, as the difference with the participants' median.

| Patient | VOI | Volume (mL) | CT density (g/mL) | Diff. CT mass | Diff. volume × 1.00 | Diff. volume × 1.06 |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| A | Liver | 2055 | 1.050 | +6.4 % | +11.8 % | +5.5 % |
| A | Liver (no lesions) | 1941 | 1.051 | -41.2 % | -38.2 % | -41.7 % |
| A | Spleen | 276 | 1.038 | -3.6 % | +0.1 % | -5.6 % |
| A | Kidney_L | 249 | 1.015 | -2.3 % | -0.8 % | -6.4 % |
| A | Kidney_R | 260 | 1.016 | -2.5 % | -1.0 % | -6.6 % |
| A | Kidneys (total) | 509 | 1.015 | -3.6 % | -2.1 % | -7.7 % |
| A | Lesion1 | 116 | 1.028 | -3.8 % | -1.1 % | -6.7 % |
| A | Lesion2 | 4 | 1.044 | -4.5 % | -0.3 % | -6.0 % |
| B | Liver | 1620 | 1.052 | +1.9 % | +7.2 % | +1.1 % |
| B | Liver (no lesions) | 1599 | 1.052 | -3.6 % | +1.4 % | -4.3 % |
| B | Kidney_L | 92 | 1.012 | -0.1 % | +1.0 % | -4.7 % |
| B | Kidney_R | 190 | 1.019 | -2.1 % | -0.2 % | -5.8 % |
| B | Kidneys (total) | 283 | 1.017 | +0.3 % | +2.0 % | -3.8 % |
| B | Lesion1 | 13 | 1.043 | -3.1 % | +1.1 % | -4.6 % |
| B | Lesion2 | 4 | 1.055 | -2.0 % | +3.4 % | -2.5 % |
| B | Lesion3 | 74 | 1.032 | -2.8 % | +0.2 % | -5.4 % |
| B | Lesion4 | 25 | 1.005 | -0.2 % | +0.3 % | -5.4 % |

- The CT density of the VOIs other than the liver is 1.005–1.055 g/mL (kidneys about 1.015: low HU and fat at the edges). Going from 1.00 to 1.06 g/mL changes the dose by 6 %, as much as the participants' spread (QCD 3–7 %).
- For the kidneys, spleen and lesions, the difference with the median is -4.5 to +0.3 % with the CT mass, -2.1 to +3.4 % with volume × 1.00, and -7.7 to -2.5 % with volume × 1.06: with a density of 1 g/mL, radot is close to the median.
- The liver does not follow (B: closer to the median with 1.06 g/mL, or with 1.00 g/mL without the lesions): the median likely mixes mass conventions and liver definitions.
- The CT computation itself is not a source of difference: resampling the CT with or without smoothing, or computing the mass on the original CT grid, changes the organ masses by less than 0.5 %.
- radot keeps the CT mass (patient-specific). The difference with the median is a convention, not an error of the dose calculation.

## T4: time integration and dose from the serial SPECT/CT

- **Input**: the 4 SPECT (Bq/mL) and the organ and lesion VOIs of each time point (no registration needed: each VOI is drawn on its own scan). Patient A's images are decay-corrected to the injection (`decay_correction` `admin`): radot brings them back to the activity at each acquisition time.
- **Time integration**: `radot integrate`, one TIA per VOI, with each method below (4 time points: with the noise level estimated, `f2` has a standard error and `f4a` none; no model selection, the AICc needs more points).
- **Dose**: organs, `radot dose -m svalue` on the TIA table (mass from the CT of time point 1, as T5); lesions (no S-value), the radot T5 `ldm` dose of the VOI scaled by the TIA ratio T4 / T5 map (marked *).
- **TIA vs map**: radot TIA vs the TIA of the challenge map in the same VOI (the map is the organisers' time integration, the T5 input).
- **Fit after**: `radot dose -m ldm --dose-rate` at each time point with the CT of that time point, then `radot integrate` on the 4 dose-rate images (VOI mean dose rate weighted by the masses of that time point, `--ct`), with the same method. Every VOI, organs and lesions (LDM, no S-value).

| Method | `radot integrate` |
|---|---|
| f2 | `--model f2` `--error-model proportional` |
| f4a | `--model f4a` `--error-model proportional` |
| trapezoid ramp/phys | `--model trapezoid` `--head ramp` `--tail phys` |
| trapezoid extrap/fit2 | `--model trapezoid` `--head extrap` `--tail fit` `--tail-points 2` |

Findings:

- Inside the participants' interquartile range (VOIs without the liver of A): `f2` 8 / 14, `f4a` 11 / 14, `trapezoid ramp/phys` 6 / 14, `trapezoid extrap/fit2` 10 / 14; fit after: `f2` 10 / 14, `f4a` 10 / 14, `trapezoid ramp/phys` 4 / 14, `trapezoid extrap/fit2` 13 / 14.
- Fit after vs fit first (both LDM; fit first: `ldm*`), over the same VOIs: `f2` -9 to +10 %; `f4a` -10 to +16 %; `trapezoid ramp/phys` -10 to +14 %; `trapezoid extrap/fit2` -10 to +14 %. The engine is linear in activity: the difference comes from the geometry of each time point. The organ masses change by 8 to 23 % between scans (each VOI is drawn again on each scan), and the fit after carries this change into the dose-rate curve. A tail fitted on two close points (`extrap/fit2`, patient A: 21 h between the last two scans) amplifies it: for the liver of A, +11 % of mass between scans 3 and 4 gives -30 % of dose (fit after vs fit first). The geometry of each time point is more exact only when the VOIs are consistent between scans.
- `f4a` (uptake then washout) is the closest to the participants for the lesions and the kidneys of B; `f2` (no uptake) underestimates the VOIs whose uptake is still visible at the first scan.
- `trapezoid ramp/phys` overestimates every VOI: the physical-decay tail ignores the biological clearance after the last scan (as on the [synthetic curves](9_validation_time_integration.md)); a fitted tail (`extrap/fit2`) removes most of it.
- The challenge TIA map and the participants differ: for some lesions the map TIA is far from radot while the radot dose is at the participants' median. The map is one time integration among others, not a reference.
- Refused (radot does not extrapolate silently): A Liver (no lesions) (trapezoid extrap/fit2): ROI 'Liver': Tail fit on the last 2 points slower than the physical decay (Teff 222.3 h > T_phys 159.5 h): use tail 'phys'.

## What this validates

- The **dose step** on real images: TIA image as input, VOI masses from the CT, OpenDose S-values with mass scaling, local deposition, and an external Monte Carlo dose-rate map (`--dose-rate-map`).
- Agreement with the community: radot falls in the narrow spread of the T5 participants (QCD 3–7 % for these targets).
- The **time integration** on real serial SPECT/CT (T4): `radot integrate` per VOI, fit first (TIA, then `radot dose` on the table) and fit after (LDM dose rate at each time point with its CT, then integrated).

## What this does not validate

- **Segmentation** (T1): not yet done.
- **Accuracy**: the participants' median is not a ground truth; a common bias of the participants and radot would not be seen.
- **Lesion doses with S-value methods**: no S-values for lesions.

## Data and how to run

The images and VOIs are from the University of Michigan [Deep Blue collection](https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/data/collections/hm50ts030) (CC BY-NC 4.0, research only). They are not redistributed: download the zips by hand, see [`validation/snmmi/`](https://github.com/dsarrut/radot/tree/main/validation/snmmi).

> We acknowledge Yuni Dewaraja at the University of Michigan for providing access to Lu-177 patient imaging data and segmentations obtained with support from R01EB022075 awarded by NIBIB and R01CA240706 awarded by NCI, NIH. Data were shared via the University of Michigan Deep Blue Data sharing repository.

```bash
python validation/snmmi/prepare_data.py    # extract the zips and convert to NIfTI
python validation/snmmi/run_gate.py        # optional: OpenGATE dose-rate maps (needs opengate)
python validation/snmmi/t5.py              # T5 doses, writes results/t5_radot.json
python validation/snmmi/t4.py              # T4 integrate + doses, writes results/t4_radot.json
pytest validation/snmmi                    # tests (T4, T5 skipped without the data)
python validation/snmmi/report.py          # regenerate this page
```
